ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=48^\circ$, the angle bisectors of the exterior angles $\angle DAC$ and $\angle ACF$ intersect at point E. What is the measure of $\angle AEC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since the bisectors of exterior angles $\angle DAC$ and $\angle ACF$ of the triangle intersect at point E, \\
it follows that $\angle CAE + \angle ACE = \frac{1}{2}(\angle B + \angle ACB) + \frac{1}{2}(\angle B + \angle BAC)\\
= \frac{1}{2}(\angle BAC + \angle B + \angle ACB + \angle B)\\
= \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ + 48^\circ)\\
= 114^\circ$\\
In $\triangle ACE$, $\angle AEC = 180^\circ - (\angle CAE + \angle ACE)\\
= 180^\circ - 114^\circ\\
= \boxed{66^\circ}$

Because CF is the extension of CB, the exterior angle ∠ACF = 180° - C; CE bisects ∠ACF, so ∠ACE = (180° - C)/2. In triangle AEC, ∠AEC = 180° - [∠CAE + ∠ACE] = 180° - [(180° - A)/2 + (180° - C)/2]. Also A+B+C=180°, and B=48°, so A+C=132°. Therefore ∠AEC = 180° - [360° - 132°]/2 = 180° - 114° = 66°.
